datasets.label: Fly HD ring (hemibrain)
datasets.summary: 130 neurons in the *Drosophila* central complex that encode the fly's heading direction. Persistent bump that tracks turns.
datasets.biology: The HD (head-direction) ring lives in the central complex (CX) of the fly's brain -- specifically the ellipsoid body (EB) and protocerebral bridge (PB). EPG neurons tile the EB and form a ring-attractor topology: a single localised bump of activity marks the fly's current heading. PEN cells inject angular-velocity input that shifts the bump when the fly turns. Delta7 neurons provide broad inhibition that stabilises the bump shape. The circuit was first characterised by Seelig & Jayaraman 2015 (Nature) and Kim et al. 2017 (Science). What you're seeing is rate-model activity (one number per neuron per timestep) on each neuron's EM-traced skeleton from the hemibrain dataset.

scenarios.label: Bump tracking
scenarios.description: A rotating Gaussian stimulus (omega = 1 rad/s) drives the EB ring; the bump should follow the stimulus with a small phase lag. This is the canonical Kim et al. (2017) test.

scenarios.label: Bump existence
scenarios.description: Stationary input centred at theta = pi/2. A localised bump should form at the input centre within ~100 ms.

scenarios.label: Bump persistence (stim then off)
scenarios.description: Static stimulus for 300 ms then removed. Activity is sustained after the input goes away (the bump's amplitude persists, though its position drifts slightly toward a network attractor).

scenarios.label: Velocity integration: left-PEN pulse
scenarios.description: Establish a bump, then pulse left-hemisphere PEN cells. The bump shifts in one direction -- this is the asymmetric loop that lets the fly integrate angular velocity.

scenarios.label: Velocity integration: right-PEN pulse
scenarios.description: Same as the left-PEN scenario but pulsing right-hemisphere PEN cells. The bump should move in the opposite angular direction.

scenarios.label: LIF spikes: rotating stim
scenarios.description: Same hemibrain HD ring, but simulated with a leaky integrate-and-fire model: neurons have voltages that spike when they cross threshold, are reset, and refract for 2 ms. Activity shown is instantaneous spike rate.

datasets.label: Fly mushroom body (subset)
datasets.summary: ~200 Kenyon cells + APL from the *Drosophila* mushroom body. Sparse coding via global inhibition.
datasets.biology: The mushroom body (MB) is the fly's olfactory learning centre. Each odour activates a small fraction (~5%) of the ~1900 Kenyon cells (KCs) in hemibrain. This sparse code is enforced by APL (anterior paired lateral) -- a single GABAergic neuron that pools activity across all KCs and inhibits them in turn. The circuit is feedforward in the excitatory direction (projection neurons -> KCs -> mushroom-body output neurons), with APL providing the only recurrent loop. We show a random subsample of 20 KCs per subtype (~200 KCs) plus APL, both with APL intact and with APL's outgoing synapses ablated, to show APL's role.

scenarios.label: Sparse coding (APL intact)
scenarios.description: Drive 30% of Kenyon cells with constant input. APL pools KC activity and inhibits in return, producing k-WTA sparse coding: only a few percent of KCs remain active at steady state.

scenarios.label: APL ablated (no inhibition)
scenarios.description: Same input drive as the previous scenario, but APL's outgoing synapses are silenced. Without global inhibition, KC activity stays dense -- demonstrating APL's role in sparse coding.

datasets.label: Human DTI brain · HCP NAP_001 (real)
datasets.summary: 94-region human DTI connectome from a real diffusion-MRI scan (HCP subject NAP_001), parcelled with AAL2.
datasets.biology: Real diffusion-MRI tractography from one Human Connectome Project subject. The 94 nodes are cortical and subcortical regions in the Automated Anatomical Parcellation 2 (AAL2, Rolls et al. 2015 NeuroImage); edge weights are streamline counts between parcels. Data shipped via the neurolib project (NAP_001 subject under neurolib's gw/ dataset). The same Galvani pipeline that runs the single-cell hemibrain HD ring runs on this region-level matrix with zero changes -- Subgraph -> Parameterizer -> Simulator is agnostic to whether each 'neuron' is one cell or one cortical parcel. Regions are rendered as small 6-spoked stars at their MNI centroids.

scenarios.label: Drive visual cortex → propagation
scenarios.description: REAL human DTI connectome (94 AAL2 regions, HCP subject NAP_001 via the neurolib dataset). Drive the visual-cortex regions; activity propagates into the rest of the brain through real white-matter streamline counts.
